01

Implementation scope

Use the application and ingestion examples together to protect sensitive fields before they reach model services.

This guide follows the supplied code and explains the configuration and integration work needed for an end-to-end RAG flow. The web repository contains the React interface and Spring Boot backend; the ETL repository prepares documents for a separate retrieval or training system.

CapabilityWhat the supplied implementation does
Web request protection ImplementedThe active generateText path calls textInputWithPrependPrompt2, combines the request with simulated relational context and a weather service response, and protects that context before Gemini generation.
Output masking demonstration ImplementedThe llmouputsimulator value is protected and revealed separately, then appended to the generated answer. The active path does not inspect and reveal the whole real LLM response.
Vector retrieval Integration requiredAlternative methods demonstrate embeddings and vector retrieval. Some are stubs or simulations; the BigQuery path contains dataset/table placeholders and is not the active request method.
Batch preparation ImplementedThe script extracts file paths from DDC NDJSON, converts supported documents, invokes protection and archives the generated list.
Indexing and model training Integration requiredThe batch script ends after protection and list archival. Chunking, embeddings, loading, retrieval access filters and training are separate integrations.
02

Repository and component map

Repository areaFiles or classesResponsibility
Fullstack UIgenai-frontend/src/App.jsCollect prompt, user ID, API key, optional JWT and simulated sensitive output. Send JSON to the backend and display the processed prompt and answer.
Fullstack APIgenai-backend/src/main/java/com/thales/genai/controller/GenAIController.javaExpose POST /api/generate-text, assemble context and invoke model and protection helpers.
Fullstack securityconfig/ApiKeyProvider.java, AuthenticationFilter.java, JwtUtils.javaResolve CSM references, compare API keys and verify a supplied JWT.
Detection and taggingGCPContentProcessor.java, ContentProcessor.java in each Java projectInspect text, map findings to policies, replace values and parse tagged protected values for reveal.
Protection adaptersThalesRestProtectRevealHelper.java, ThalesCADPProtectRevealHelper.javaCall the configured REST service or CADP implementation.
Retrieval examplesdb/VectorDbHelper.java, service/BigQueryService.java, service/SnowflakeJDBCService.javaProvide example data access paths. Verify which method is selected before treating an integration as active.
ETL orchestrationthales-genai-ddc-processor.sh, watch_and_run_ddc_protect.shRun the preparation stages; optionally watch a Linux directory for incoming reports.
ETL stagesExtractFilesFromDDCReport2Linux, ConvertToTextBatchProcessorFileList, ThalesGCPProtectRevealBatchProcessorGenerate a file list, convert content, and process text/CSV in protect or reveal mode.

Controller and configuration paths are relative to com/thales/genai in the fullstack backend. ETL Java classes are under src/main/java without a package declaration.

03

Prepare services and access

  • Build tools: JDK 17 or higher, Maven, and Node.js/npm compatible with the frontend package. The web backend declares Java 17. Resolve the required Thales SDK dependencies for the ETL build.
  • Google Cloud: a project with access to the selected Gemini model and DLP inspection, API enablement and service permissions appropriate to the deployment. Supply Application Default Credentials or an approved workload identity to the Java processes.
  • CipherTrust: working policies, keys, user/access policies and either CRDP connectivity or a configured CADP client. Confirm the policy names used by both projects exist.
  • Secrets: CSM connectivity and a restricted application identity that can read the required paths. Deliver its bootstrap credentials securely.
  • Source data: a DDC NDJSON export and readable source files. A discovery report identifies files; it does not transfer their contents to the processing host.
  • Batch execution: Bash for the orchestration script. Linux directory watching additionally requires inotifywait and completed-file delivery handling.

Decide which environments may process raw content. DLP inspection receives the submitted text; the application, conversion directories and protection components also see raw values before protection. Restrict those locations and their logs accordingly.

04

Configure detection and protection policies

Both projects load thales-config.properties from the classpath. For source builds, edit the copy under src/main/resources and rebuild. Editing a similarly named file beside the JAR does not override the bundled resource in these examples.

Map information types to policies

The following excerpt shows the shared mapping pattern. Policy names are examples that must match your CipherTrust configuration. Use an explicitly authorized reveal identity in place of demo-user.

POLICYNAME=char-internal
POLICYTYPE=internal
DEFAULTPOLICY=char-internal
SHOWMETADATA=true
TAGPREFIX=ENC
REVEALUSER=demo-user
TAG.nbr=nbr-internal
TAG.char=char-internal
TAGCODE.nbr=RU5DbmJy-
TAGCODE.char=RU5DY2hhcg==-
PII.PERSON_NAME=TAG.char
PII.STREET_ADDRESS=TAG.char
PII.EMAIL_ADDRESS=TAG.char
PII.PHONE_NUMBER=TAG.nbr
PII.US_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER=TAG.nbr
PII.DATE_OF_BIRTH=TAG.char
PII.CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER=TAG.nbr

PII.EMAIL_ADDRESS=TAG.char resolves through TAG.char to the char-internal protection policy. Numeric information types map to nbr-internal. The Java inspection list is hard-coded separately: adding a new PII.* property alone does not enable a new detector.

Understand the detection threshold

The processors request DLP findings at POSSIBLE likelihood or higher, but only protect findings whose numeric likelihood is greater than 3. Consequently, some returned findings are counted as skipped and remain unprotected. Review this decision using representative data, including names, multiline content and context-dependent values.

Understand the protected representation

Base64(TAGPREFIX + tagName) + "-" + protectedLength + ":" + protectedValue

ENCchar -> RU5DY2hhcg==
ENCnbr  -> RU5DbmJy

The prefix identifies which policy mapping to use during reveal. Base64 encodes the tag; it is not the cryptographic protection. CipherTrust protects the value. Although comments refer to a byte count, the code records Java String.length() and later slices Java strings, so the length is measured in UTF-16 code units.

Keep the parser and policy format aligned

The reveal parser recognizes the two example prefixes and strips a three-character tag prefix. Renaming TAGPREFIX or adding tag families requires parser changes as well as properties changes. The code also infers internal policy mode from the policy name containing “internal”; validate this convention when introducing policies.

05

Configure the application and its secrets

In the web backend, ApiKeyProvider reads the following environment variables at startup. Several names contain paths to CSM secrets, not the final configuration values.

VariableMeaning in this implementation
CSM_URLCSM/Akeyless API base URL used by the client.
CSM_ACCESSID and CSM_ACCESSKEYBootstrap credentials used to authenticate to CSM; protect delivery and restrict their permissions.
CSM_SECRETPath to a JSON secret. The current parser uses its first entry: the entry key becomes the application API key and the entry value becomes the encoded JWT public key.
VERTEXAI_LOCATIONPath to the secret whose value is the model location.
VERTEXAI_MODEL_NAMEPath to the secret whose value is the model ID.
PROJECTIDPath to the secret whose value is the Google Cloud project ID.
CRDPIP and CRDPPORTDirect host and port configuration for the web REST helper. The port defaults to 8090.
MYDEBUGApplication debug flag; defaults to false. Other source-level debug printing is not consistently controlled by this flag.

The unusual API-key/public-key JSON structure is specific to this sample. A production configuration should use explicit named fields and a validated schema rather than depend on the first JSON entry.

Model selection and retirement

Update the value of the secret referenced by VERTEXAI_MODEL_NAME, then restart the backend so it reloads configuration. Select a currently available model in a supported location and verify project access. A NOT_FOUND error can indicate an unavailable model, a location mismatch or missing access. Check the Google model lifecycle and location documentation before deployment.

CSM keeps managed secret values out of normal application configuration, but the process still holds resolved secrets in memory. The batch example separately reads CADP-related settings from its properties resource; it does not use this web backend CSM loader.

06

Run and trace the web application

Build and start

With services, credentials and environment variables configured, run the backend and frontend in separate terminals. The examples below use Bash syntax.

git clone https://github.com/markbwarner/my-fullstack-genai-app.git
cd my-fullstack-genai-app/genai-backend
mvn clean package
mvn spring-boot:run
cd my-fullstack-genai-app/genai-frontend
npm install
npm start

In genai-frontend/src/App.js, the local fetch target is http://localhost:8085/api/generate-text. Set it to the backend URL appropriate to the browser environment. A deployed browser interprets localhost as its own machine. Configure CORS for the intended frontend origin.

Trace the active request

  1. AuthenticationFilter requires a matching X-API-Key before continuing. It then attempts to verify an optional bearer JWT and attaches its email claim to the request.
  2. GenAIController.generateText chooses that email when available, otherwise it uses the submitted userId. It validates that the prompt and chosen user ID are non-empty.
  3. The controller selects textInputWithPrependPrompt2. This method combines simulated account context, a weather service result and the user's prompt.
  4. GCPContentProcessor.processText inspects the combined text and replaces selected findings with policy-tagged protected values.
  5. The method builds a Gemini model with a system instruction and calls generateContent using the protected base context. It returns newPrompt and generatedText.
  6. The controller separately protects and reveals llmouputsimulator under the configured policy and appends the result to the generated answer.
The combined prompt is the protection boundary

Inspect every field that can enter the model request, including retrieved passages, service responses, attachments and dynamic instructions. The active method protects the base context; separately supplied system instructions need their own review if they become data-dependent.

Test the API

The following uses fictional data. Set RAG_API_KEY in the terminal through your approved secret-delivery method. Use the real backend route or the gateway route configured for your deployment.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8085/api/generate-text \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: ${RAG_API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "Summarize the issue for Alex Morgan at alex.morgan@example.com",
    "userId": "demo-user",
    "llmouputsimulator": "Synthetic confidential output for the masking demonstration"
  }'

A JWT can be added using Authorization: Bearer <token>, while retaining the required API key. Inspect newPrompt to verify that expected findings were protected; do not assume every name will pass the configured detection threshold. The field name llmouputsimulator contains the spelling used by the code.

Interpret the output demonstration

The simulator applies the configured protection policy to the supplied string, then requests reveal using the selected user identity. Depending on policy, the displayed result may be cleartext or masked. This demonstration does not prove that the actual generated answer has been scanned for sensitive content.

07

Run the document preparation pipeline

The batch flow starts with a DDC NDJSON report. Run DDC discovery and export outside the script. The processing host must be able to read the files named by the report.

Build and configure the batch project

The supplied local project is E:\eclipse-workspace\thales.csp.genai-etl.example. Set its classpath properties before building, including the CipherTrust policy mappings and CADP connection settings. The active batch code creates ThalesCADPProtectRevealHelper using KEYMGRHOST and CRDPTKN. Resolve the Thales dependency declared in the POM and the required client configuration.

cd /path/to/thales.csp.genai-etl.example
mvn clean package

The script expects thales.csp.genai-etl.example-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar in its working directory. Set its JAR_FILE variable to the actual runnable dependency-containing JAR under target. Check the build output, since a shaded artifact may have a different name.

Stage 1 Extract the file list

ExtractFilesFromDDCReport2Linux reads each NDJSON record, joins path and name, and writes the resulting paths to a list. The first non-empty record supplies datastoreName, used to name ddc.<datastoreName>.output.txt. This extractor does not independently classify or filter files; the exported report must represent the intended input set.

Stage 2 Convert documents

ConvertToTextBatchProcessorFileList processes paths from that list. It supports PDF, Word DOC/DOCX, Excel XLS/XLSX, and text/CSV. PDF and Word content become text; spreadsheets become CSV; text and CSV inputs are copied. Source files remain separate from converted outputs.

The parser does not establish general OCR support for scanned PDFs or image-only documents. Check extracted content before declaring a document ready for protection. Conversion files are still raw data and need a restricted staging area.

Stage 3 Inspect and protect

ThalesGCPProtectRevealBatchProcessor processes top-level .txt and .csv files in the converted directory. In protect mode it invokes DLP inspection and CipherTrust protection; in reveal mode it parses tags and calls reveal. Output filenames add .protected or .revealed before the final extension.

Run the combined workflow

bash thales-genai-ddc-processor.sh \
  /data/reports/ddc-export.ndjson \
  /data/rag/run-001 \
  protect \
  your-gcp-project-id

The four arguments are report path, base output directory, mode and Google Cloud project ID. The script creates this directory structure:

/data/rag/run-001/
  ddc/                 # generated file list before archival
  converted/           # raw extracted text and CSV
  protected/           # protection output; validate before use
  processed-ddc-data/  # archived file list after processing

The final move archives the generated list, not the original documents. Use a fresh base output directory for each run so stale converted files cannot be processed again or mixed into a later load.

Run each Java stage separately
java -cp "$JAR_FILE" ExtractFilesFromDDCReport2Linux \
  /data/reports/ddc-export.ndjson /data/rag/run-001/ddc

java -cp "$JAR_FILE" ConvertToTextBatchProcessorFileList \
  /data/rag/run-001/ddc/ddc.example.output.txt \
  /data/rag/run-001/converted

java -cp "$JAR_FILE" ThalesGCPProtectRevealBatchProcessor \
  protect /data/rag/run-001/converted \
  /data/rag/run-001/protected your-gcp-project-id

Set JAR_FILE to the built JAR path and replace the illustrative list filename with the actual name printed by the extractor.

08

Connect protected data to retrieval

The next component consumes validated protected output. Keep this handoff explicit so raw or partially processed data cannot enter the embedding or model path.

  1. Validate and approve files. Reconcile source, conversion and protection manifests; check failures and missed fields before making output available.
  2. Chunk protected text. Preserve document IDs, provenance, version, tenant and access metadata. Keep a tagged value intact when splitting text.
  3. Generate embeddings. Send protected chunks to the selected embedding model. Store vectors with the corresponding protected text and metadata.
  4. Implement retrieval. Replace simulator or stub methods with a real vector or hybrid query. Enforce document and tenant authorization before passing retrieved content onward.
  5. Protect query-time context. Apply the same detection and policy conventions to user input and additional service/database context. Ensure protection runs before any embedding or summarization call that must not receive raw values.
  6. Generate and handle responses. Supply authorized retrieved context, inspect real model output, and reveal only the values and representation permitted for the authenticated user.

Exact matches and semantic search

For exact matching of protected values, confirm that protection is deterministic for the selected policy and key scope, and normalize values consistently. Use compatible policy versions and coordinate key changes. Do not assume that encrypting the same cleartext in two systems always produces the same representation.

For semantic search, encrypted names and identifiers do not preserve their original meaning. Use useful non-sensitive descriptive context and evaluate relevance, precision and recall. Re-embed and re-index as needed after changes to protection, chunking or the embedding model.

Identify the selected code path

textInputWithRAGAndVectorDB and related methods illustrate retrieval and intermediate summarization. Audit each intermediate model call as well as the final call. textInputWithRAGAndVectorDBBigQuery constructs VectorDbHelper with placeholder dataset/table names. Switch methods only after configuring and testing that path. The active controller currently selects textInputWithPrependPrompt2.

Do not use the LLM to recover protected values

The trusted application and CipherTrust service perform authorized reveal. A system instruction asking the model to preserve protected strings can help formatting, but cannot guarantee the model will reproduce tags or protected values exactly. Validate returned representations before reveal.

09

Enforce identity and response handling

Establish a trusted reveal identity

The sample prefers a verified JWT email when present, but otherwise accepts userId from the request body. In production, bind reveal identity to the authenticated principal and its server-side entitlements. Reject attempts to choose a more privileged identity in the payload.

JwtUtils verifies signatures and parses claims. Add explicit checks for expected issuer, audience and required identity claims. The API filter rejects an absent or wrong API key before JWT handling; bearer-only authentication is not supported by the current control flow.

Make state local to the request

The controller mutates revealUser on a shared static helper. Concurrent requests can overwrite one another's identity. Use an immutable request context or a per-request helper so the reveal identity and policy cannot cross request boundaries.

Process the real model response

Integrate inspection of the actual LLM answer and a controlled parser for protected spans. Apply reveal only to validated protected values under the trusted identity. Encode output for its rendering context and validate structured values before downstream tools or database use.

If the model alters a tag, length or protected payload, reject or safely withhold that span. Keep source identifiers so the application can recover an approved value from a trusted store when necessary, rather than relying on model-generated ciphertext.

Test different policy outcomes

Use at least two authenticated test users: one entitled to full reveal and one receiving the configured masked result. Include denied access and malformed representation cases. The UI simulator is useful for this demonstration, while integration tests must also cover actual model output.

10

Protect endpoints and operational data

Route browser requests through the configured Imperva WAF/API Security endpoint when that layer is deployed. The backend controller route is /api/generate-text. A public route such as /redact/generate-text requires an explicit gateway rewrite to the backend route; changing the fetch URL alone does not configure that mapping.

  • Use HTTPS for public traffic and an authenticated encrypted connection or protected service channel for CRDP. The sample REST helper constructs an HTTP URL.
  • Limit origin access so clients cannot bypass the gateway. Configure CORS, API schema controls, request size limits and rate limits for the application.
  • Disable logging of raw prompts, DLP quotes, API keys, CRDP request bodies and revealed data. Some helper classes print these values independently of MYDEBUG.
  • Restrict raw and converted staging files and set retention/cleanup procedures. Encrypting source storage does not replace field protection before a model call.
  • Audit protection and reveal decisions using request IDs, policy identifiers and outcomes, without copying sensitive values into telemetry.

These controls support defense in depth. A WAF does not replace model-context protection, document authorization or policy-based reveal.

11

Validate the end-to-end result

TestExpected evidence
Known sensitive samplesRepresentative email, phone, identity and financial samples are protected as expected; missed or skipped findings are reviewed.
Model and embedding boundaryCaptured test requests show only approved protected content at every model call, including intermediate summaries and embeddings.
Authentication and authorizationMissing/wrong API keys fail; invalid JWTs do not grant privileges; body user IDs cannot escalate reveal permissions.
Two simultaneous usersConcurrent requests retain their own reveal identities and receive only their authorized policy outcome.
Service failureDLP/CRDP/CADP outages prevent unprotected submission and incomplete output publication.
ETL fidelityFiles with spaces, repeated basenames, multiple sheets, malformed records, scanned PDFs and mixed Unicode are either processed correctly or explicitly quarantined.
Retrieval quality and isolationRelevant results remain useful after protection; cross-tenant and unauthorized documents cannot be retrieved.
Actual model outputSensitive model output is inspected; malformed tags are handled safely; rendered content and downstream actions are validated.
Logs and stagingNo API keys, raw findings or revealed content appear in routine logs; staging retention and access policies are enforced.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCheck
Gemini NOT_FOUNDResolve the model secret, location and project access in ApiKeyProvider. Confirm a supported model, then restart.
401 from the APICheck X-API-Key against the value resolved from CSM. A JWT alone does not bypass the API-key requirement.
Sensitive text remains visibleCheck extraction quality, the hard-coded information type list, policy mapping and likelihood threshold. Also check whether a protection call failed.
Reveal cannot parse a valueCheck the tag family, configured prefix, stored length, policy version and whether the LLM changed the representation.
No documents convertedCheck the DDC list, mounted source paths, whitespace handling, supported extensions and filesystem permissions.
The UI cannot reach the APICheck the browser-visible host, CORS, backend port, TLS and gateway path rewrite.

Sources and implementation references

The architecture and implementation descriptions draw on the supplied Protecting-rag.docx and the two example codebases. Code behavior described here reflects the local source reviewed on November 9, 2026.

  1. Fullstack GenAI example — React UI, Spring Boot API, data protection helpers, authentication and example retrieval integrations.
  2. GenAI ETL example on the genaibatch branch — DDC report extraction, document conversion and batch protection. The local ETL checkout is the implementation reference for this guide.
  3. Google Cloud explanation of RAG — retrieval, grounding and external knowledge sources.
  4. OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 — risk names and numbering used in these documents.

For direct code review, start with GenAIController, ApiKeyProvider and the ETL orchestration script. Local changes may differ from the published branches.
